body.x: Korea Lighting Inc. (CEO Dongwoo Lee) participated on Tuesday, December 9, in the “Global Media Meetup” hosted by AVING News’ International Press Club (IPC) for domestic companies and startups at MIK Basecamp in Seocho-gu, Seoul.

The Global Media Meetup focuses on introducing Korean companies’ and startups’ products and technologies to the global market. In particular, it aims to proactively report on CES 2026 Innovation Award winners and CES-participating startups through global media channels and expand business opportunities.

Founded in 2010, Korea Lighting positions itself as a “functional opto-semiconductor platform company,” developing solutions that go beyond illumination to improve human health and quality of life through light. Its core proprietary technology, HS FRAME, integrates LED chips, circuits, and heat sinks into a single structure, reducing thermal resistance to 1.75 K/W. The company explained that this innovation overcomes the heat limitations of conventional LEDs and enables stable medical-grade high-output wavelengths.

Based on this proprietary platform technology, Korea Lighting has developed the ambient brain healthcare device Neurélux, the beauty wellness brand Lümedique, and sterilization hygiene lighting, positioning itself as a leader in the bio-healthcare market.

body.cap: Product image of Neurélux | Image provided by Korea Lighting

body.x: Korea Lighting has received New Excellent Technology (NET) and New Excellent Product (NEP) certifications from the Korean government, as well as the Jang Young-sil Award, recognizing its technological excellence. The company has also secured global intellectual property rights with patents registered in seven countries, including the United States, Japan, and Europe. Its flagship hygiene lighting product, Vitamin LED, was designated as an innovative product by the Public Procurement Service and has been adopted by more than 300 domestic public institutions, fire stations, and hospitals, demonstrating its performance and safety.

The company has also commercialized smart farming solutions by applying HS FRAME packaging technology to agriculture, achieving more than a 50% efficiency improvement compared with conventional lighting. At the same time, it is accelerating entry into the U.S. and Japanese markets with beauty and healthcare devices. In particular, starting with CES 2026, Korea Lighting plans to accelerate expansion into B2C and B2B2C markets through the global launch of its brain healthcare solution Neurélux.

Neurélux applies HS FRAME semiconductor thermal management technology to reduce thermal resistance, enabling stable, medical-grade high-output wavelengths without noise or vibration. The device offers an innovative non-contact brain healthcare solution that eliminates the inconvenience of conventional wearable devices that must be worn on the body.

By presenting a new approach to preventing and managing age-related dementia and sleep disorders—two of the biggest challenges of ultra-aging societies—through everyday light, Neurélux connects directly to global problem-solving. Its minimalist ambient design departs from the cold aesthetics of hospital medical devices and blends naturally into everyday spaces such as bedrooms and living rooms.

body.cap: Examples of Neurélux in use | Image provided by Korea Lighting

body.x: Korea Lighting stated, “We are positioning CES 2026 as the strategic debut stage for the global launch of Neurélux. Through the world’s first ‘Ambient Brain Healthcare’ category, we aim to reshape the wearable-centric photobiomodulation market and secure technological leadership.”

The company added, “Through this participation, we expect to establish strategic partnerships with major healthcare buyers and companies in North America and Europe, demonstrate that Korea Lighting’s functional opto-semiconductor technology represents a new global standard in digital healthcare, and achieve tangible export contracts along with expanded global brand recognition.”

Korea Lighting identified the U.S. home healthcare and sleep tech markets as its top priority targets. Beginning with the global launch of Neurélux in March 2026, the company plans to pursue strategic collaborations with leading U.S. home healthcare companies to expand its presence in North America. It also plans to initiate global clinical trials to verify therapeutic efficacy and further strengthen Neurélux’s technological credibility.

Technologically, Korea Lighting is developing a follow-up lineup that manages the entire “Neurovascular Axis,” extending from the brain to the spine and nervous system, using its core HS FRAME technology. Through this strategy, the company aims to go beyond device manufacturing and evolve into an “ambient PBM platform” company that extends healthy human lifespan and leads the future of non-invasive longevity technology.

body.x: Meanwhile, AVING News has introduced Korean companies to the world through partnership cooperation with more than 800 media outlets across 54 countries over the past 22 years. Building on its long-established global media network, AVING News launched the International Press Club in August. Media outlets participating in this Global Media Meetup included Innovation & Tech Today from the United States, Le Café Du Geek from France, Arageek from the United Arab Emirates, and Digitimes from Taiwan.
